newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CANBERRA WATCH-And they doubted the Bank's judgement.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CANBERRA WATCH-And they doubted the Bank's judgement.

text.p: Canberra Watch feels compelled to observe what few people are gracious enough to say: that the Reserve Bank has been vindicated yet again.
Remember how the bank surprised the economic community with the first monetary easing of the current round?
Oh how some doubted the bank's judgement! It was too soon, some said. It was probably not needed at all, said others.
There were dark murmurs that it would all have to be reversed before long.
Well, if anything, it is now clear that July 31 monetary easing was perhaps a little late, although almost no-one made that complaint on July 31.
The bank has confirmed the wisdom of its initial action with today's second easing, the need for which is generally accepted in the economic community.

Before that, recall the three 1994 tightenings. Those adjustments were so well judged that the bank did not have to touch the levers for a gloriously prolonged 19 months. The 1994 growth bubble subsided and inflation remained controlled.
Canberra Watch always thought it was a pity that, as everyone argued through 1995 whether the next move would be up or down, no one was congratulating the bank for creating such a stable environment.
And finally, one recalls the long series of monetary easings, from 18 percent cash to 4.75 percent between 1990 and 1993.
It seemed every second easing was called "political" by commentators who judged that the economy was about to burst into a rampant inflationary phase at any minute.
Very few in the economic community urged the bank to move faster, especially in the critical period of 1990 and 1991, when we can now see that that was exactly what it should have been doing.

The bank's call then was hardly perfect -- and it may not be in the current round of easings -- but the point is that its judgement has been very good, at least as good as the median view in the market.
